blind_target.authors: Gillies, J. C. P., & Dozois, D. J. A.
blind_target.title: How long do mood induction procedure (MIP) primes really last? Implications for cognitive vulnerability research.
blind_target.evidence_quote: The two dissertation studies aimed to test the reproducibility of findings from the original study (Gillies, 2018; Gillies & Dozois, 2021) by conducting an exact replication and extending the study design to address the three additional questions listed above.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Statistical analyses of data from these studies revealed results that largely support findings from the original study. That is, the MIPs were often ineffective for a substantial percentage of participants and induced sadness diminished quickly, often within 6 min.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The lay summary gives an overall supportive verdict across both studies. The thesis and subsequent article report the same original sample, but the thesis uniquely reports the latent growth analyses; both are explicitly retested.
